ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: On the left side of the figure, there is an R group connected to the α carbon; this α carbon is also connected to the carboxylic acid group C(=O)OH above, and is connected through HN to a transition-state central carbon. After ignoring the curved arrows, the central carbon is connected to a methyl group, a hydroxyl group O-H, and an acetyl group O-C(=O)CH3 connected through oxygen. Reasoning: write the unspecified R connection point as *; starting from the α carbon gives *C(...)C(=O)O; the amino substituent on the α carbon is written as N, and N continues to connect to the central carbon. The substitution form of the central carbon is C(C)(O)OC(C)=O. Combining gives the SMILES: *C(NC(C)(O)OC(C)=O)C(=O)O.

method.method_draft: Convert the visual molecular graph directly into SMILES. Start at the unspecified R attachment as '*' connected to the alpha carbon: '*C(...)C(=O)O'. Put the alpha carbon's amino substituent in a branch: N is bonded onward to the transition-state carbon. Encode that N-substituted carbon as C(C)(O)OC(C)=O because it has methyl, hydroxyl, and acetoxy branches. Combine these pieces to obtain '*C(NC(C)(O)OC(C)=O)C(=O)O'.
